Cedar School Systems is a fictional company. This independent exercise does not mean the C# learning path is complete: that path's content is still coming soon. No real internship, employer, AI review, grade, payment or certificate is provided.

Client problem: a fictional school tracks students, teachers and classes in separate lists. Build a small C# console application that keeps these records consistent and makes class rosters easy to find.

Requirements and scope Use C# classes for students, teachers, class groups and enrollments, with unique IDs. Add, view, edit and remove student and teacher records with input validation. Create class groups, assign a teacher, enroll students and display class rosters without duplicate enrollments. Explain and enforce what happens when deleting a referenced student, teacher or class. Save and reload local JSON data. Handle missing and malformed files explicitly. Use fictional records only; do not include real children's data, credentials or personal information.

Required deliverables A GitHub repository containing your C# console project and fictional sample data. A README with prerequisites, setup/run commands, model explanation and usage examples. A checklist of manual tests and their actual results, plus known limitations. Automated tests may be included if you write them.

Suggested implementation steps Review the requirements and design the model and menus. Implement record management, class assignment and enrollment validation. Add JSON persistence and error handling. Run your checks locally, document limitations and save your repository link below. Use the sample review as a checklist, revisit the requirements and update your link or notes when needed.

Sample review — prepared checklist This is a Sample review, not a review of your submitted solution. These notes are the same for everyone and do not depend on your repository, task states or submission. The system has not read any code.

Read the prepared sample review Check that IDs remain unique after editing records and reloading saved data. Try duplicate enrollments, invalid menu input and deletion of a teacher with assigned classes. Test startup without a JSON file and with a malformed file. Explain how existing data is protected. Make sure another learner can follow the README to run the app. Record what is incomplete instead of treating a Done label as proof of correctness. Review the requirements before updating your solution
